ctl.sd1: Option 1 – hotkey (no plugin): On the Stream Deck, drag the “Hotkey” action onto a key and enter a key from F13 to F24 (no keyboard has those, so no conflict with iRacing). Then click “Assign” next to the action above and press the Stream Deck key.
ctl.sd2: Option 2 – web address: With the free Stream Deck plugin “Web Requests” (BarRaider, in the Stream Deck store) call one of these addresses (method GET). This also opens any display directly:
ctl.h1: Set iRacing to “Borderless Window” under Options → Graphics. In exclusive fullscreen, Windows can't draw overlays on top of the game.
ctl.h2: For OBS: Add source → Browser, paste the overlay's address and set a matching size (Relative 430×300, Standings 640×460, Inputs 600×110, Delta 380×130, Dashboard 860×500, Radar 220×300 – adjust to your rows/columns).
ctl.h3: Closing this window doesn't quit the program – it keeps running in the taskbar notification area.
ctl.h4: All overlays are plain HTML/CSS files in the resources/web folder and may be adapted for your own use (modified versions must not be shared).

ctl.updInfo: dbDash downloads the update, closes briefly and restarts. Your settings are kept; your own changes to the overlay files (resources\web) will be overwritten. Best not during a race.
ctl.updConfirm: Update dbDash to version {v} now and restart?
ctl.diagSub: If times or gaps look wrong: records 60 seconds of iRacing data (includes the drivers' names of the session). You can send the file to the developer.
ctl.diagNoData: No data – please record during a session in iRacing.
